name: Linz oxygen-steel production
summary: In November 1952 the VÖEST works at Linz began making steel by blowing pure oxygen onto molten iron, the LD process that became the world's main steelmaking method.
description: An operating LD plant converted carbon-rich hot metal into lower-carbon steel by oxygen blowing.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.
why: Postwar Austria needed flat steel quickly, and cheap tonnage oxygen made blowing oxygen rather than air practical.
